questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 40.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

options.A: They all have a capsid made of protein.

questions.questionText: Samples of glucose, sucrose, and a mixture of glucose and sucrose were divided into two halves M and N. M was then tested with Benedict’s solution. N was boiled with dilute hydrochloric acid, neutralised and then tested with Benedict’s solution. The colour of the solution was compared to colour standards. Which table identifies the correct colour changes for these samples?

options.A: B sample M N sample M N glucose blue blue glucose yellow yellow sucrose blue yellow sucrose blue yellow mixture blue yellow mixture blue yellow
options.C: D sample M N sample M N glucose yellow yellow glucose yellow red sucrose blue yellow sucrose blue red mixture yellow red mixture yellow red

questions.questionText: Some foods contain hydrogenated vegetable fats. These are unsaturated fats that have been converted to saturated fats. Which property of the fats will have changed?

options.A: Their hydrocarbon chains will fit together more closely.
options.B: Their solubility in water will increase.
options.C: They will have more double bonds in their molecules.
options.D: They will remain liquid at room temperature.

questions.questionText: A polypeptide contains a specific number of amino acids, n. How many peptide bonds are present in this polypeptide?

options.A: n – 1 B n C n + 1 D n + 2

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct?

options.A: Amylase, ribose and phospholipid are all macromolecules.
options.B: Cellulose, glucose and catalase are all polymers.
options.C: Deoxyribose, fructose and ribose are all monosaccharides.
options.D: Sucrose, deoxyribose and amylopectin are all polysaccharides.

questions.questionText: A student used colorimetry to monitor the hydrolysis of a protein by a protease enzyme. The student used biuret solution to determine the concentration of protein in the hydrolysis reaction. The student produced a calibration curve using known concentrations of protein. Which diagram shows the calibration curve?

options.A: B transmission absorbance 0 0 0 protein 0 protein concentration concentration
options.C: D transmission absorbance 0 0 0 protein 0 protein concentration concentration

questions.questionText: A student completed an experiment to measure how increasing concentrations of substrate affects the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction. The student then repeated the experiment after adding a fixed quantity of a reversible competitive inhibitor. Which row describes the effect of a reversible competitive inhibitor on enzyme activity? attachment of inhibitor effect of increasing substrate concentration at active site on rate of enzyme-controlled reaction

options.A: no little effect on the rate
options.D: yes little effect on the rate

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a liposome. Liposomes can be used to move therapeutic drugs into cells of the body to treat conditions such as cancer. Which row shows the property of a drug that could be transported in the sections of the liposome labelled 1 and 2? property of drug property of drug transported in location 1 transported in location 2

options.A: hydrophilic hydrophilic

The blocks were submerged in acid. All other variables were kept constant. The time taken for each of the blocks to completely turn yellow was recorded. Which of the four blocks became completely yellow most quickly?
Which processes require mitosis?
Which events listed are part of the cell cycle?
Telomerase is an enzyme that adds nucleotides to telomeres. Which statement about telomerase is correct?

options.A: A high concentration of telomerase in a cell damages genes during DNA replication.
options.B: A high concentration of telomerase in cancerous cells limits the rate of tumour growth.
options.C: The low concentration of telomerase in stem cells means that these cells can divide an unlimited number of times.
options.D: The low concentration of telomerase in body cells means that these cells can divide a limited number of times.

questions.questionText: Bacterial cells with DNA containing only the ‘heavy’ isotope of nitrogen (15N) are allowed to reproduce for three generations in a culture medium containing the normal isotope of nitrogen (14N). Which percentage of the DNA molecules produced contain strands with the heavy isotope of nitrogen? first generation second generation third generation % % %
A bacterial circular DNA molecule is 2600150 base pairs long. 26% of the bases are adenine. How many cytosine bases would be in the DNA molecule?
Which statement relating to the structure of DNA is correct?

options.A: Two DNA strands are joined to each other by phosphodiester bonds.
options.B: The alignment of bases to form a double helix is only achieved between antiparallel strands.
options.C: Three hydrogen bonds are formed between all base pairs containing purines.
options.D: The number of cytosine bases always equals the number of thymine bases.

questions.questionText: What is systolic blood pressure?

options.A: the blood pressure in the arteries when the heart is relaxing
options.B: the blood pressure in the left ventricle at the start of a contraction
options.C: the maximum blood pressure in the arteries
options.D: the maximum blood pressure in the right ventricle

questions.questionText: The diagram shows pressure changes in the left side of the heart and aorta over time. The length of this cardiac cycle is 0.6s. Points 1, 2, 3 and 4 indicate when atrioventricular valves and semilunar valves either open or close.
Which reactions take place in the capillaries surrounding an alveolus?
Which statement explains the importance of the chloride shift in red blood cells (RBC)?

options.A: Carbon dioxide diffuses from blood plasma into RBC and chloride ions diffuse out of RBC to maintain a balance of positive and negative ions.
options.B: Hydrogencarbonate ions diffuse into plasma from RBC and chloride ions diffuse into RBC to maintain a balance of positive and negative ions.
options.C: Carbon dioxide in RBC together with chloride ions stimulate the release of oxygen from haemoglobin to allow increased levels of respiration.
options.D: Hydrogencarbonate ions diffuse into RBC from plasma and chloride ions diffuse into plasma to maintain a balance of positive and negative ions.
